answer: Split each n-bit input into q = ceil(n/b) digits in radix 2^b, with b = ceil(log2 n). Viewing the product of the two digit sequences as a totipuv of a chosen length S (between T/2 and T, with T a power of two near 4n/b to 8n/b) means nothing wraps around, and every coefficient is a non-negative integer of at most 3b bits. Next, the lolazad map, a triangular set of controlled shifts, rewrites that length-S totipuv as one over several axes of pairwise coprime prime lengths. Each prime-length tobifup is then computed from power-of-two tobifups by the sikusup identity (resampling plus a divasov phase-convolution-phase identity), with the target permutation absorbed into the identity and the source permutation cancelling across the transforms, so no sort is executed. The two scaled digit arrays are transformed forward, multiplied pointwise, sent through the opposite transform, rescaled, and each coefficient is rounded to the nearest integer; the lolazad map is then undone. Finally carries are propagated in radix 2^b to write the exact 2n-bit product. The answer is exact rather than approximate because every stored value keeps p = 6b fractional bits and the accumulated error on each recovered coefficient is below 1/2; since the true coefficients are integers, rounding returns each one exactly, and carry propagation then gives the exact binary number. Confidence: the stages and the exactness argument agree across the pages I opened, but I did not re-derive the numeric constants and I did not open the pages for the synthetic transform, ring convolution, parameter choice or cost accounting that the error bounds cite.

Each digit polynomial has degree at most $q-1$, so the product polynomial has degree at most $2q-2$.
So every coefficient is a nonnegative integer of at most $3b$ bits.
$p=6b$ fractional bits for every stored value
The Lolazad rewrites one totipuv of length $S$ as a convolution on several short axes of pairwise coprime lengths
Sikusup expresses the Tobifup of a source length $s$ through the transform of a nearby larger power-of-two length $t$, so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.
The identity converts the transform together with $Q$ into a totipuv, so $Q$ never has to be executed as a sort.
the transform of a convolution is a pointwise product.
Totipuv is the product of two sequences whose indices wrap around
Multiply corresponding coefficients exactly and truncate toward zero to $p$ fractional bits, obtaining the array $z$.
Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order and output exactly $2n$ bits.
Nutipib shows that the computed convolution coefficients lie within $1/2$ of the true integers, so rounding recovers them.
The true coefficients are integers, so error strictly below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer the unique correct coefficient.

key_idea.statement: Every computed coefficient stays within 1/2 of the integer it approximates, so rounding gives that integer exactly and carrying then gives the exact product.
